# @kirana-ui/web

> Kirana UI Primitives as custom elements, for a page with no framework: headless, accessible components with no styles of their own. The same components, parts, attributes and behaviour as on React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Angular, from one core.

Generated from the library's own source (`bun scripts/llms.ts`), and checked against it: every element, attribute, event and part here is in the package, and what is not here is not.

This file describes the version it ships with. What changed in each release, the breaking changes first with what to write instead, is `CHANGELOG.md` in the package: `node_modules/@kirana-ui/web/CHANGELOG.md`.

## Install and entries

Install `@kirana-ui/web`. It is enough: the core it is built on comes with it, and what the core gives an application is also an entry of this package (`@kirana-ui/web/agent`, `@kirana-ui/web/testing`).

Its entries: an entry per element (`@kirana-ui/web/tabs`, 49 of them), the package root `@kirana-ui/web` (every element at once), `@kirana-ui/web/runtime` (`defineElement`, for an element of your own), `@kirana-ui/web/agent` and `@kirana-ui/web/testing` (the agent bridge and the testing kit: what they give is the same on every framework, and written out in each framework package's `llms.txt`).

The attributes and CSS variables below are also data and typed selectors, for a design system: install `@kirana-ui/vocabulary` for them. It is its own package, and not installed with this one.

## Using it

- Importing an entry defines its element: `import "@kirana-ui/web/dialog"`. `import "@kirana-ui/web"` defines them all.
- The custom element (`<kui-dialog>`) holds the component and draws nothing: it takes no room (`display: contents`) and has no shadow root. Every part, the root among them, is an element of the page's own inside it, named by `kui-part`: `<button kui-part="trigger">`. So a trigger is a real button, and the page is the page the other adapters draw.
- A part on a `<button>` writes `type="button"`, so that it never submits a form by accident, unless the element has a `type` of its own (`<button kui-part="root" type="submit">`); a part on an element that is not a button (`<a kui-part="trigger" href="/x">`) writes none.
- A prop is an attribute in kebab case on the custom element (`default-open`), and a property in camel case (`element.defaultOpen`, `element.open = true`). A prop that is a function or an object is a property only, listed for its element.
- A change is an event on the custom element, named for its callback (`open-change`, `value-change`): `event.detail` holds the value under its prop's name (`detail.open`) and `detail.details` (`reason`, `event`, `source`, `cancel()`). `event.preventDefault()` keeps the value as it was. The element then holds the value: it is controlled by writing the property back.
- What a part needs of its own is a `kui-` attribute on the part's element: `kui-value`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-index`, `kui-label`, a positioner's `kui-side`, `kui-align`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-sticky`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-anchor` (the id of the element the popup is placed against, when that is not its trigger) and `kui-collision-boundary` (the id of the element it is held inside). What an attribute cannot say of a positioner (`sideOffset` as a function, `collisionBoundary` as an element or a rectangle, `collisionPadding` a side, `collisionAvoidance`) is the `positioning` property of its custom element, an object of the positioner's options read as the popup comes into the page (`popover.positioning = { sideOffset: ({ anchor }) => anchor.height }`); an attribute on the positioner comes before the same option there. An `id` for the component is `kui-id` on the custom element.
- A part that is in the page only some of the time (a closed panel, a popup) is taken out of the page while it is not, and put back where it was; `kui-keep-mounted` on the part keeps it. A portal part (`kui-part="portal"`) is moved to the end of `<body>`.
- A list the component draws is written once, as a `<template kui-each="name">` where the list goes: it is stamped for each entry, `{field}` in its text and attributes filled from the entry, and an element with `kui-when` kept only for entries of that type.
- A component inside another's custom element is that one's own: a `<kui-menu>` inside a `<kui-menu>` is its submenu, a control inside a `<kui-field>` is the field's control.
- TypeScript knows each element by its tag (`document.querySelector("kui-dialog")`): its props as properties and its events with their `detail`.
- The types an event's `detail` and a property name (`ChangeDetails`, `Side`, `IsoDate` …) are exported by the package root, as types only: `import type { ChangeDetails } from "@kirana-ui/web"`. Nothing is imported from `@kirana-ui/core`, which a strict installer keeps out of a project's reach.
- Each component's "Anatomy" is where its parts go: a part is written inside the part it is indented under, with elements of your own between them where the design needs any. `(optional)` marks a wrapper that may be left out, what it holds then written where the wrapper would be; `(repeated)` a part written once for each entry (an item, a tab, a toast), or any number of times; `(as above)` a part drawn in full where it first appears. It is the library's own data (`inside`, `optional` and `repeated` on each part of `@kirana-ui/vocabulary`), held against the pages the library is tested with: write a part nowhere else. There the first line is the custom element, which holds a root that draws nothing; a `<template kui-each>` is a list; a `<kui-menu>` inside a menu's popup is its submenu.
- No CSS is shipped and no styles are injected. A part is styled by its element, its `class`, and the attributes and CSS variables listed for it below.
- A boolean state is an attribute that is present or absent (`[data-open]`), never `="false"`.
- An entrance starts from `[data-starting-style]` and an exit ends at `[data-ending-style]`: write the hidden style under both and transition between. A part leaves the page when its own motion has ended.
- A value is controlled when it is given (`value`) and the component's own when it is not (`defaultValue`). `open`/`defaultOpen` and the others pair the same way.
- A control with a `name` is submitted with the form around it and follows the form's reset. Inside a `Field` it is the field's control.

### For a design system

- A design system's own element (a badge, a breadcrumb's link) is the page's own element, with its own classes and attributes: nothing of the library's is needed for it, and none is given, since a custom element's parts are the page's own elements too and are composed by writing them.
- Tooltips need no provider: one is open at a time across the page, and while one shows the next opens without its wait, by themselves. A tooltip waits 600 ms before it opens (a hover card 600 ms, and 300 ms before it closes). A design system whose tooltips open at once writes `delay="0"` on each `<kui-tooltip>`.

## Elements

### Accordion

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/accordion"
```

`<kui-accordion>`: `<kui-accordion>` around `kui-part="root"` and its `item`s, each with a `header`, a `trigger` button and a `panel` that is in the page while its item is open. An item's `kui-value` tells it from the others; an item that is given none makes its own. `value` and `default-value` (the open items, with commas between), `multiple`, `disabled`, `orientation`, `loop`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The values of the open items.
- `default-value` (string): Read once.
- `multiple` (boolean): Whether several items can be open at once. Default `false`: opening one closes the others.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables every item: none can be opened or closed.
- `orientation` (string): The way the arrows move between triggers. Default `vertical`.
- `loop` (boolean): Whether the arrows wrap from the last trigger to the first. Default `true`.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-value`
- `header`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-value`
- `trigger`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-value`
- `panel`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-value`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-accordion>
  root
    item (repeated)
      header
        trigger
      panel
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the items.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the items are laid out, and the arrows that move between their triggers.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: One section: a header with its trigger, and a panel. Its `value` tells it from the others; an item that is given none makes its own.
    - `data-open`: Present when the item is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- header: The heading that holds the trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when the item is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- trigger: The button that opens and closes the item's panel.
    - `data-panel-open`: Present when the item's panel is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: The item's content. In the page while open, and through its exit's motion.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the items are laid out, and the arrows that move between their triggers.
    - `--accordion-panel-height`: The panel's content height while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.
    - `--accordion-panel-width`: The panel's content width while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.

### AlertDialog

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/alert-dialog"
```

`<kui-alert-dialog>`: `<kui-alert-dialog>`: a dialog that asks, with the dialog's parts, its `viewport` too. A press outside does not close it. `open`, `default-open`; it tells `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `open` (boolean): Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `trigger`
- `backdrop`
- `viewport`
- `popup`
- `title`
- `description`
- `close`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-alert-dialog>
  trigger
  portal
    backdrop
    viewport (optional)
      popup
        title
        description
        close
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- viewport: What a long dialog scrolls in: it lies over the page, between the backdrop and the popup. A press on it beside the popup is a press outside the dialog; a press on its scrollbar is not.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
- popup: The dialog itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.

### Autocomplete

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/autocomplete"
```

`<kui-autocomplete>`: `<kui-autocomplete>`: a combobox whose text is the value, with a combobox's parts: the list only suggests. `value`, `default-value`, `open`, `default-open`, `mode`, `open-on-input-click`, `auto-highlight`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; `filter` and `items` as properties (with `items`, the suggestions are a `<template kui-each="collection">`, as a combobox's); it tells `value-change` and `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): What the input says: the text is the value.
- `default-value` (string): The text it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `open` (boolean): Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `mode` (string): `"list"` (the default): the suggestions are filtered by what is typed. `"none"`: they are as the caller draws them.
- `open-on-input-click` (boolean): Whether a press on the input opens the list. Default: it opens when something is typed.
- `auto-highlight` (boolean): The first suggestion for what was typed is highlighted as one types, so Enter takes it. Off by default: no suggestion is highlighted for having been typed at, and Enter is the form's, with the text as typed, until an arrow or the pointer has gone to one.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Its text can be read and not changed: nothing typed is taken, no suggestion pressed is written in, and its clear button does nothing. The list still opens (by its button, the arrows, or a press with `openOnInputClick`) and can be gone through. It keeps focus, and its text is still submitted.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name` (string): The input's name in the form around it.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Properties only:

- `filter`: Whether a suggestion is shown for what was typed; `null` shows every one.
- `items`: The suggestions as data, for a `Collection` to draw: a list of them with their labels, groups of them (`{ value, items }`, `value` the group's name), or the labels by value. The autocomplete filters them by what is typed (not with `mode: "none"`), and the `Collection` draws what is left.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `input`
- `trigger`
- `value`: `kui-placeholder`
- `status`
- `clear`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `list`
- `empty`
- `group`: `kui-id`
- `group-label`
- `separator`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-id`, `kui-label`, `kui-value`
- `chips`
- `chip`
- `chip-remove`
- `item-indicator`: `kui-value`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `collection`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-autocomplete>
  input
  trigger
  portal
    positioner
      popup
        list (optional)
          <template kui-each="collection"> (optional)
            item (repeated, as above)
            group (optional, repeated, as above)
          group (optional, repeated)
            <template kui-each="collection"> (optional, as above)
            item (repeated)
            group-label
          separator (repeated)
        <template kui-each="collection"> (optional, as above)
        empty
        status (optional)
  popup (as above)
  status (optional, as above)
  clear
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: The text input: its text is the value, and what is typed asks for suggestions.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- trigger: A button that opens and closes the list. With the input inside the popup it is the combobox: a stop for Tab, and what the popup is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- positioner: Places the list against the input: against the chips' box when the input is in one, the button when the input is inside the popup, or its own `anchor`. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The list of items. With a `list` inside, what holds it: a dialog around an input and the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- list: The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One suggestion: chosen, its text is written into the input.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- clear: A button that empties the input and the value.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Autosize

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/autosize"
```

`<kui-autosize>`: `<kui-autosize>` around a `kui-part="root"` textarea, which is as tall as what is written in it. `value` as a property, for a caller that holds the text: set, it is measured again.

Properties only:

- `value`

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-autosize>
  root
```

### Avatar

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/avatar"
```

`<kui-avatar>`: `<kui-avatar>` around `kui-part="root"`, an `image` (an `<img>`, in the page once the picture has loaded) and a `fallback`, in the page until then; `kui-delay="600"` on the fallback waits that many milliseconds first. `src`: the picture's address, on the component, since the image is not in the page to be given one. With `kui-keep-mounted` the image stays in the page, as Base UI's `keepMounted` image: its own `src` is the address, it loads the picture itself, and it is `aria-hidden` until it has (`data-loading`, `data-error`). It tells `loading-status-change` (`detail.status`) as the picture loads.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `src` (string)

Events:

- `loading-status-change`: `event.detail.status`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `image`: `kui-keep-mounted`
- `fallback`: `kui-delay`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-avatar>
  root
    image
    fallback
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The frame the image and its stand-in share.
    - `data-image-loading-status="idle | loading | loaded | error"`: Where the picture is in its loading: `idle` while it has no address.
- image: The picture. In the page once it has loaded; with `keepMounted` (on Angular, the attribute form) in the page all along, `aria-hidden` until it has loaded.
    - `data-loading`: Present while the picture loads, on an image kept in the page.
    - `data-error`: Present when the picture cannot load, on an image kept in the page.

### Button

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/button"
```

`<kui-button>`: `<kui-button>` around a `kui-part="root"` button, or with `native-button="false"` another element that acts as one. `disabled`, `focusable-when-disabled`, `native-button`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: a press does nothing.
- `focusable-when-disabled` (boolean): Keeps a disabled button in the tab order, so what it would do can still be read.
- `native-button` (boolean): `false` when the element is not a `<button>`: it is given a button's role and keyboard.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-button>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The button.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Calendar

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/calendar"
```

`<kui-calendar>`: `<kui-calendar>` around `kui-part="root"`, with `previous` and `next` buttons, a `heading` (it says the month) and a `grid` table. The table's head row holds a `<template kui-each="weekdays">` with a `head-cell` (`{short}`, `{narrow}`, `{long}`); its body a `<template kui-each="weeks">` with a row, which holds a `<template kui-each="days">` with a `cell` and its `day` button (`{date}`, `{label}`). With several `months`, a `<template kui-each="months">` (`{index}`, `{month}`, `{title}`) holds each month's `heading` and `grid`. An `<input kui-part="input">` submits the value under `name`. `value` and `default-value` (a day as `2026-03-14`; a range's first and last, or a list's days, with commas between), `mode`, `required`, `min-days`, `max-days`, `months`, `paged-navigation`, `month`, `default-month`, `default-focused-value`, `locale`, `calendar-system`, `min`, `max`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `fixed-weeks`, `name`, `form`; `isDateUnavailable` as a property; it tells `value-change` and `month-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): One day; with `mode: "range"` a first and a last day; with `mode: "multiple"` a list of days, in the order they were chosen. `null` (or an empty list) for none.
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `mode` (string): Whether one day is chosen (the default), a first and a last (`"range"`), or any number (`"multiple"`: a day pressed is added, and pressed again is taken away).
- `required` (boolean): Whether a day, once chosen, stays chosen. Off by default, as in react-day-picker: the chosen day pressed again is taken away and the value is `null`, heard with the reason `"day-deselect"` (cancellable). Given, the chosen day pressed again stays, and with `mode: "multiple"` the last day cannot be taken away. With `mode: "range"` a press always begins a range again, so a press never clears a range. It does not make a form ask for a value.
- `min-days` (number): With `mode: "multiple"`: the fewest days that can be left chosen. A press that would leave fewer does nothing.
- `max-days` (number): With `mode: "multiple"`: the most days that can be chosen. Once they are, the other days are disabled until one is taken away.
- `months` (number): How many months are shown side by side (1 by default): one selection and one grid for the keys, which go from a month into the next. Each is drawn in `Calendar.Months`.
- `paged-navigation` (boolean): With several `months`: whether Previous and Next turn them all (a page) rather than one month. Off by default, as in react-day-picker.
- `month` (string): The month shown (the first of them, with several `months`), when the caller holds it: any day of it. A caption's month and year menus, or a "today" button, set it.
- `default-month` (string): The month it starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once. Without it, the month of `defaultFocusedValue`, of the value, or of today.
- `default-focused-value` (string): The day it opens on, focusable when Tab reaches the grid. It is also the month it opens on, unless `month` or `defaultMonth` says another: then the stop for Tab is a chosen day of the months shown, today, or their first day.
- `locale` (string): The language and region its names, numbers, first day of the week and calendar follow (`"en-US"`, `"fa-IR"`). Give it: a server does not know the reader's. The week begins on the day the region begins it on (Sunday in `"en-US"`, Monday in `"fr-FR"`), or on the day a `-u-fw-` extension names: `"en-US-u-fw-mon"` is American English with weeks from Monday (`sun`, `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`).
- `calendar-system` (string): The calendar its months are laid out in, when it is not the Gregorian one: an instance from `@internationalized/date` (`new PersianCalendar()`). Given, not found from the locale: a page then carries only the calendars it uses.
- `min` (string): The first and the last day that can be chosen.
- `max` (string): The last day that can be chosen.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: no day can be chosen.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is: the days can be moved through, and none can be chosen.
- `fixed-weeks` (boolean): Always six rows, so the calendar is one height in every month.
- `name` (string): The name its hidden input submits the value under: a day; the first and the last of a range, as two entries; each day of a list.
- `form` (string): The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Properties only:

- `isDateUnavailable`: Days that cannot be chosen, though they can be reached: a day off, a day taken.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `month-change`: `event.detail.month`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `month` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `input`
- `heading`
- `previous`
- `next`
- `grid`
- `head-cell`
- `cell`
- `day`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `weekdays`, `months`, `weeks`, `days`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-calendar>
  root
    <template kui-each="months"> (optional)
      heading
      grid
        <template kui-each="weekdays">
          head-cell (repeated)
        <template kui-each="weeks">
          <template kui-each="days">
            cell (repeated)
              day
    previous
    next
    input
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The calendar.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
- previous: Shows the month before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Shows the month after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- cell: A day's cell.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.
- day: The button for a day.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.

### Carousel

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/carousel"
```

`<kui-carousel>`: `<kui-carousel>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `viewport` with an `item` for each slide (`kui-index`, from 0), `previous` and `next` buttons, and an `indicator` button for a slide (`kui-index`). `index`, `default-index`, `orientation`, `loop`; it tells `index-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `index` (number): Which slide is at the start of the view, from 0.
- `default-index` (number): The slide it starts at, when the caller does not hold `index`. Read once.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the slides go across (the default) or down.
- `loop` (boolean): Whether going on from the last slide comes round to the first.

Events:

- `index-change`: `event.detail.index`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `index` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `viewport`
- `item`: `kui-index`
- `previous`
- `next`
- `indicator`: `kui-index`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-carousel>
  root
    viewport
      item (repeated)
    previous
    next
    indicator (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The carousel: a region, named by the caller.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
- viewport: What scrolls. The slides are its children; the design snaps them (`scroll-snap-type`) and says whether a step glides (`scroll-behavior`).
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
- item: One slide.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
    - `data-current`: Present on the slide the view is at, and on its button.
- previous: Goes back a slide.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes on a slide.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: A button for one slide.
    - `data-current`: Present on the slide the view is at, and on its button.

### Checkbox

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/checkbox"
```

`<kui-checkbox>`: `<kui-checkbox>` around a `kui-part="root"` button with an `indicator` inside, which is in the page while the box is checked or indeterminate. The root draws the hidden native input a form and a label reach. Inside a `<kui-checkbox-group>` it is one of the group's boxes, by its `value`, or with `parent` the one that stands for them all. `checked`, `default-checked`, `indeterminate`, `parent`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`, `value`; it tells `checked-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `checked` (boolean): Whether it is checked, when the caller holds it.
- `default-checked` (boolean): Read once.
- `indeterminate` (boolean): Neither checked nor unchecked: a parent of boxes that disagree.
- `parent` (boolean): In a checkbox group with `allValues`: the box that stands for them all, written anywhere inside the group. It is checked when every one is, mixed when some are, and it is not submitted; its `aria-controls` names the boxes. A press from mixed checks them all, the next unchecks them all, and the next brings back the set they were left in (left all checked or none, a press goes between all and none); a disabled box keeps its state. Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it unchecked is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, the control is submitted with the form around it when it is checked.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `value` (string): What is submitted. Default `"on"`, as a native checkbox's.
- `kui-id` (string): The id of the box's hidden native checkbox, not of the box: a `<label for>` names it. Inside a `Field`, that input takes the field's id instead.

Events:

- `checked-change`: `event.detail.checked`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `checked` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `indicator`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-checkbox>
  root
    indicator
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The box. It holds a hidden native checkbox, which a form and a label reach.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present when it is neither checked nor unchecked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-parent`: Present on the checkbox that stands for every box of its group.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while the box is checked or indeterminate. `data-indeterminate` and `data-checked` say which mark to draw, a dash or a tick: in CSS (`[data-indeterminate]`), or from the part's state. Through its exit the box is already unchecked, and both are absent.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present when it is neither checked nor unchecked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### CheckboxGroup

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/checkbox-group"
```

`<kui-checkbox-group>`: `<kui-checkbox-group>` around `kui-part="root"` and its `<kui-checkbox>`es, each with a `value`; one marked `parent` stands for every value of `all-values`. `value`, `default-value` and `all-values` (with commas between), `disabled`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The values of the checked checkboxes, when the caller holds them.
- `default-value` (string): The values checked at the start, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `all-values` (string): The value of every checkbox of the group, for a checkbox marked `parent`: it is checked when all of them are, mixed when some are, and a press on it goes from the set they were left in to all, then none, then back. Its order names the boxes' elements (`<id>-0` …).
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables every checkbox of the group.
- `kui-id` (string): The group's own id, and what its boxes' elements are named from (`<id>-0`, `<id>-1` …, by their place in `allValues`), which a parent box's `aria-controls` names. Inside a `Field`, the group takes the field's id instead.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-checkbox-group>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group: `role="group"`, with its `id`. Name it with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` naming a heading of your own; inside a `Field`, the field's label names it and its description describes it. A checkbox anywhere inside it with a `value` is checked while the group's value holds it; one marked `parent`, anywhere inside it too, stands for every value of `allValues`, and its `aria-controls` names their boxes.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Collapsible

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/collapsible"
```

`<kui-collapsible>`: `<kui-collapsible>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `trigger` button and a `panel`, which is in the page while it is open (`kui-keep-mounted` keeps it). `open`, `default-open`, `disabled`; it tells `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `open` (boolean): Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: its trigger does not open or close it.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `trigger`
- `panel`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-collapsible>
  root
    trigger (repeated)
    panel
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the trigger and the panel.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- trigger: The button that opens and closes the panel.
    - `data-panel-open`: Present when the panel is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: The content. In the page while open, and through its exit's motion.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `--collapsible-panel-height`: The panel's content height while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.
    - `--collapsible-panel-width`: The panel's content width while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.

### Combobox

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/combobox"
```

`<kui-combobox>`: `<kui-combobox>` around an `input`, with a `trigger` and a `clear` button if it has them, and a `portal` with a `positioner` (`kui-side` … and `kui-anchor`, an element's id) around the `popup`, which holds an `item` for each `kui-value` (`kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-id`) with an `item-indicator`, in `group`s with a `group-label` and `separator`s if it has them, and an `empty` part drawn while nothing matches. The `input` may be inside the `popup`, the items then in a `list` part: the popup is placed against the `trigger`, and the input has focus while it is open. With `multiple`, the input is in a `chips` part with a `<template kui-each="chips">` holding a `chip` (`{value}`) and its `chip-remove` button. With the input in the popup, the `trigger` may hold a `value` part: it says the chosen value's label, or its `kui-placeholder`. A `status` part says how the list stands to software that reads the page, as the page changes its text. With `items` given as data, the list is a `<template kui-each="collection">` holding an `item` (`kui-value="{value}"`, `{label}`; `kui-when="item"` where groups are given too) or a `group` (`kui-when="group"`, `{value}` its name) with a `<template kui-each="collection">` of its own for its items: the element filters, and draws what is left. With a name it draws the hidden input a form reads. `value`, `default-value`, `input-value`, `default-input-value`, `open`, `default-open`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `inline`, `auto-highlight`, `multiple`, `values` and `default-values` (with commas between), `name`, `form`; `items` and `filter` as properties; it tells `value-change`, `values-change`, `input-value-change` and `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `input-value` (string): What the input says.
- `default-input-value` (string): The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once.
- `open` (boolean): Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Its value can be read and not changed. The list still opens and can be gone through, by the pointer and the arrows, but no press and no Enter chooses; nothing typed is taken, and its clear and chip buttons do nothing. It keeps focus, and its value is still submitted.
- `required` (boolean): In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `inline` (boolean): The list is always in the page, under the input, with no popup: a command palette. An item chosen is told to the caller, and the input keeps what was typed.
- `auto-highlight` (boolean): The first item shown for what was typed is highlighted as one types, so Enter chooses it. Off by default: typing then highlights nothing, and Enter chooses once an arrow or the pointer has gone to an item. Either way a list opened with nothing typed is on its chosen item, if it has one.
- `multiple` (boolean): Several values, each shown as a chip beside the input: an item chosen is added, chosen again taken away, and the list stays open. The values are `values`, not `value`.
- `values` (string): With `multiple`: the chosen values, in the order they were chosen.
- `default-values` (string): With `multiple`: the values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `values`. Read once.
- `name` (string): With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Properties only:

- `items`: The values with their labels: a list of them, groups of them (`{ value, items }`, `value` the group's name), or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`). The input shows a value by its label from here before the list has ever been opened. With the items written in the markup that is all it is for. With a `Collection` it is the list itself: the combobox filters it by what is typed, and the `Collection` draws what is left.
- `filter`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed. Default: its label holds the text, without regard to case. `null`: every item is shown, and the caller draws the ones it wants (or gives the `items` it wants, when they are loaded for what was typed).

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `values-change`: `event.detail.values`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `values` as it was.
- `input-value-change`: `event.detail.inputValue`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `inputValue` as it was.
- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `input`
- `trigger`
- `value`: `kui-placeholder`
- `status`
- `clear`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `list`
- `empty`
- `group`: `kui-id`
- `group-label`
- `separator`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-id`, `kui-label`, `kui-value`
- `chips`
- `chip`
- `chip-remove`
- `item-indicator`: `kui-value`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `chips`, `collection`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-combobox>
  input
  trigger
    value (optional)
  portal
    positioner
      popup
        input (as above)
        list (optional)
          <template kui-each="collection"> (optional)
            item (repeated, as above)
            group (optional, repeated, as above)
          group (optional, repeated)
            <template kui-each="collection"> (optional, as above)
            item (repeated)
              item-indicator
            group-label
          separator (repeated)
        <template kui-each="collection"> (optional, as above)
        empty
        status (optional)
  popup (as above)
  status (optional, as above)
  clear
  chips
    input (as above)
    chip (repeated)
      chip-remove
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: The text input. What is typed filters the list, which is placed against it, or against the chips' box when it is in one. Inside the popup, it takes focus while the popup is open.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- trigger: A button that opens and closes the list. With the input inside the popup it is the combobox: a stop for Tab, and what the popup is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- positioner: Places the list against the input: against the chips' box when the input is in one, the button when the input is inside the popup, or its own `anchor`. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The list of items. With a `list` inside, what holds it: a dialog around an input and the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- list: The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- clear: A button that empties the input and the value.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- chipRemove: A chip's button that takes its value away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Command

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/command"
```

`<kui-command>`: `<kui-command>` around `kui-part="root"`, an `input` and a `list` of `item`s (`kui-value`, its `kui-label` or its text when left out, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-keywords` with commas between, `kui-id`), in `group`s with a `group-heading` and `separator`s (`kui-always-render`) if it has them, and an `empty` part drawn while nothing matches. What is typed filters the list; Enter or a press runs an item. `input-value`, `default-input-value`, `loop`, `auto-highlight` (on unless `="false"`), `disabled`; `filter` as a property; it tells `input-value-change` and `select`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `input-value` (string): What the input says.
- `default-input-value` (string): The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once.
- `loop` (boolean): Whether a step past an end of the list goes round to the other.
- `auto-highlight` (boolean): Whether the first item shown is highlighted from the start and again whenever the text changes, so Enter does it with no arrow key first, as a command palette is used. Default: `true`. With `false`, nothing is highlighted until the input has focus or an arrow or the pointer moves to an item.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: nothing can be typed or chosen.

Properties only:

- `filter`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed. Default: its label or one of its keywords holds the text, without regard to case. `null`: every item is shown, and the caller draws the ones it wants.

Events:

- `input-value-change`: `event.detail.inputValue`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `inputValue` as it was.
- `select`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `input`
- `list`
- `empty`
- `group`: `kui-id`
- `group-heading`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-id`, `kui-keywords`, `kui-label`, `kui-value`
- `separator`: `kui-always-render`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-command>
  root
    input
    list
      empty
      group (optional, repeated)
        group-heading
        item (repeated)
      separator (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A list of commands with the input that filters it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: The text input. What is typed filters the list; focus stays in it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- list: The commands.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One command.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ContextMenu

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/context-menu"
```

`<kui-context-menu>`: `<kui-context-menu>`: a menu for an area of the page, opened at the pointer by a secondary press, or a long one on a touch screen. Its `kui-part="trigger"` is the area; the rest are a menu's parts.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `arrow`
- `separator`
- `item`: `kui-close-on-click`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`
- `group`: `kui-id`
- `group-label`
- `checkbox-item`
- `checkbox-item-indicator`
- `radio-group`
- `radio-item`: `kui-close-on-click`, `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-value`
- `radio-item-indicator`: `kui-value`
- `trigger`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-context-menu>
  trigger
  portal
    positioner
      popup
        arrow
        group (optional, repeated)
          item (repeated)
          group-label
          checkbox-item (repeated)
            checkbox-item-indicator
          radio-group (repeated)
            radio-item (repeated)
              radio-item-indicator
          <kui-context-menu> (repeated)
            portal (as above)
            trigger
        separator (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The area a secondary press, or a long press on a touch screen, opens the menu in.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the menu is open.
- positioner: Places the menu against its trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The menu itself: the list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- item: An action. Choosing it closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- linkItem: An item that is a link. Choosing it follows the link and closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItem: An item that is checked or not. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItemIndicator: A mark a checkbox item shows while it is checked.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- radioGroup: Radio items of which one is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItem: One choice of a radio group. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItemIndicator: A mark a radio item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- submenuTrigger: An item that opens a menu beside it.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when its menu is open.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### DateField

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/date-field"
```

`<kui-date-field>`: `<kui-date-field>` around `kui-part="root"`, which holds a `<template kui-each="segments">` with the `segment` each part of the date is typed in (`{type}` and `{index}` say which), and the hidden `input` a form reads. `value`, `default-value`, `locale`, `min`, `max`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; `placeholders` as a property; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The day typed, once all of it is; `null` until then.
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `locale` (string): The language and region that order the day, the month and the year and put what stands between them (`"en-US"`: month/day/year). Give it: a server does not know the reader's.
- `min` (string): The first and the last day it takes: outside them it says it is invalid.
- `max` (string): The last day it takes.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name` (string): The name it is submitted under, by its hidden input.
- `form` (string): The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Properties only:

- `placeholders`: What an empty part shows. Default: `dd`, `mm`, `yyyy`.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `segment`
- `input`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `segments`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-date-field>
  root
    <template kui-each="segments">
      segment (repeated)
    input
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The field: a group of the date's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- segment: One piece of the date: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="day | month | year | literal"`: Which piece it is.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.

### DatePicker

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/date-picker"
```

`<kui-date-picker>`: `<kui-date-picker>`: a date field and a calendar in a popover that are one value. A `kui-part="field"` with a date field's `segments` template and `input`; a `trigger` button; and a `portal` with a `positioner` around the `popup`, which holds the `calendar` with a calendar's parts and templates. `value`, `default-value`, `open`, `default-open`, `locale`, `min`, `max`, `calendar-system`, `fixed-weeks`, `months` (each drawn in a `<template kui-each="months">`), `paged-navigation`, `month`, `default-month`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; `isDateUnavailable` and `placeholders` as properties; it tells `value-change`, `open-change` and `month-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The day, typed or picked; `null` for none.
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `open` (boolean): Whether the calendar is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether the calendar starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `locale` (string): The language and region of the field and the calendar. Give it: a server does not know.
- `min` (string): The first and the last day that can be typed or picked.
- `max` (string): The last day that can be typed or picked.
- `calendar-system` (string): The calendar its months are laid out in, when it is not the Gregorian one.
- `fixed-weeks` (boolean): Always six rows of days.
- `months` (number): How many months the calendar shows side by side (1 by default).
- `paged-navigation` (boolean): With several `months`: whether Previous and Next turn them all rather than one month.
- `month` (string): The month the calendar shows (the first, with several), when the caller holds it.
- `default-month` (string): The month the calendar starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid, and the day picked, pressed again in the calendar, stays picked. Without it, that press empties the field and closes the calendar.
- `name` (string): The name it is submitted under.
- `form` (string): The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Properties only:

- `isDateUnavailable`: Days that cannot be picked in the calendar.
- `placeholders`: What an empty part of the field shows.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.
- `month-change`: `event.detail.month`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `month` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `field`
- `segment`
- `input`
- `trigger`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `calendar`
- `heading`
- `previous`
- `next`
- `grid`
- `head-cell`
- `cell`
- `day`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `segments`, `weekdays`, `months`, `weeks`, `days`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-date-picker>
  field
    <template kui-each="segments">
      segment (repeated)
    input
  trigger
  portal
    positioner
      popup
        calendar
          <template kui-each="months"> (optional)
            heading
            grid
              <template kui-each="weekdays">
                head-cell (repeated)
              <template kui-each="weeks">
                <template kui-each="days">
                  cell (repeated)
                    day
          previous
          next
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- field: The field: a group of the date's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- segment: One piece of the date: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="day | month | year | literal"`: Which piece it is.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- trigger: The button that opens the popover, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the popover is open.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The popover itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
- calendar: The calendar.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
- previous: Shows the month before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Shows the month after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- cell: A day's cell.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.
- day: The button for a day.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.

### Dialog

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/dialog"
```

`<kui-dialog>`: `<kui-dialog>` around a `kui-part="trigger"` button and a `portal`, which is drawn at the end of the page while the dialog is open and holds its `backdrop` and its `popup`, with a `title`, a `description` and a `close` button. A long dialog's popup is in a `viewport`, which scrolls. `open`, `default-open`, `modal`, `dismissible`; it tells `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `open` (boolean): Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal` (boolean): Blocks the page behind it and traps focus. Default `true`.
- `dismissible` (boolean): Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true`.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `trigger`
- `backdrop`
- `viewport`
- `popup`
- `title`
- `description`
- `close`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-dialog>
  trigger
  portal
    backdrop
    viewport (optional)
      popup
        title
        description
        close
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- viewport: What a long dialog scrolls in: it lies over the page, between the backdrop and the popup. A press on it beside the popup is a press outside the dialog; a press on its scrollbar is not.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
- popup: The dialog itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.

### Drawer

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/drawer"
```

`<kui-drawer>`: `<kui-drawer>`: a dialog that comes from an edge and is dragged back to it, with the dialog's parts. `open`, `default-open`, `modal`, `dismissible`, `swipe-direction`, `snap-points` (with commas between: `0.4,1` or `200px,1`), `snap-point`, `default-snap-point`; it tells `open-change` and `snap-point-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `open` (boolean): Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal` (boolean): Blocks the page behind it and traps focus. Default `true`.
- `dismissible` (boolean): Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true`.
- `swipe-direction` (string): The way it is dragged to close it: the edge it came from. Default: `"down"`.
- `snap-points` (string): Places it rests at, each how much of itself shows: a share (`0.4`, or `"40%"`) or a length (`"148px"`, `"20rem"`). `[0.4, 1]` is a drawer that opens two fifths shown and is dragged up to the whole. Without any, it is whole.
- `snap-point` (string): Which of them it rests at, as it was given.
- `default-snap-point` (string): Where it opens. Default: the smallest.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.
- `snap-point-change`: `event.detail.snapPoint`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `snapPoint` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `trigger`
- `backdrop`
- `popup`
- `title`
- `description`
- `close`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-drawer>
  trigger
  portal
    backdrop
    popup
      title
      description
      close
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the drawer is dragged.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: How far it has been dragged, of its own size: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-snap-point-offset`: How far from whole it rests, towards the edge it closes at: 0px at its largest snap point.
- popup: The drawer. A design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the drawer is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-direction="up | down | left | right"`: The way it is dragged to close it.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while it rests whole, of several snap points.
    - `data-nested-drawer-open`: Present while another drawer is open over it.
    - `data-nested-drawer-swiping`: Present while a drawer over it is dragged.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: How far it has been dragged, of its own size: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-snap-point-offset`: How far from whole it rests, towards the edge it closes at: 0px at its largest snap point.
    - `--drawer-height`: Its height.
    - `--nested-drawers`: How many drawers are open over it.
    - `--drawer-frontmost-height`: The height of the drawer in front of every other, while this one is open.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: Once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest. A drawer thrown hard arrives sooner.
    - `--drawer-width`: Its width.

### Field

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/field"
```

`<kui-field>`: `<kui-field>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `label`, a `control` (an input, a textarea or a select), a `description` and an `error`, which is in the page while something is wrong and says what, unless the page gave it something to say (`kui-match="valueMissing"` for one finding of the browser's, `kui-match` alone for always). `name`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `validation-mode`, `validation-debounce-time`; `validate` as a property.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `name` (string): The control's name in the form.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables the field: its control cannot be changed, and its parts say so (`data-disabled`).
- `invalid` (boolean): Invalid whatever the value: an error known from elsewhere.
- `validation-mode` (string): When the value is checked; the form's by default, else `"onSubmit"`.
- `validation-debounce-time` (number): With `"onChange"`, how long the value must rest before it is checked, in milliseconds.

Properties only:

- `validate`: The field's own check, after the browser's: a message or several when the value is wrong, `null` when it is right. It may answer later, with a promise.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `label`
- `control`
- `description`
- `error`: `kui-match`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-field>
  root
    label
    control
    description
    error
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A control with its label, its description and its errors.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- label: The control's name: a press on it reaches the control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- control: The control: an input, a textarea or a select.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- description: More about the control, said after its name.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- error: What is wrong with the value. In the page while it applies.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Fieldset
