```
    frame
      pattern
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the code.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the value is longer than a code holds.

### RadioGroup

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/radio-group"
```

`<kui-radio-group>`: `<kui-radio-group>` around `kui-part="root"` and an `item` button for each `value`, with an `indicator` inside that is in the page while its item is the chosen one. An item draws the hidden native radio a form and a label reach; an item's `kui-id` is that radio's id, which a `<label for>` names. `value`, `default-value`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables every item of the group.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, choosing none is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, the chosen value is submitted with the form around the group.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-id`, `kui-value`
- `indicator`: `kui-value`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-radio-group>
  root
    item (repeated)
      indicator
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the items: one of them is chosen at most.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
- item: One choice. It holds a hidden native radio, which a form and a label reach: the item's `id` (`kpId` on Angular, `kui-id` on a custom element) is the radio's, which a `<label for>` names.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while its item is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Resizable

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/resizable"
```

`<kui-resizable>`: `<kui-resizable>` around `kui-part="group"`, its `panel`s (`kui-default-size`, `kui-min-size`, `kui-max-size`, in shares of a hundred) and a `handle` between two (`kui-disabled`). `orientation`, `keyboard-step`, `disabled`; it tells `sizes-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `orientation` (string): Whether the panels are side by side (the default) or one over the other.
- `keyboard-step` (number): How far an arrow key moves a handle, in hundredths of the group. Default: 10.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: the handles cannot be dragged or moved with the keyboard.

Events:

- `sizes-change`: `event.detail.sizes`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `group`
- `panel`
- `handle`: `kui-disabled`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-resizable>
  group
    panel (repeated)
    handle (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- group: The panels and the bars between them. A design lays it out as a flex box: `display: flex`, and `flex-direction: column` when it is vertical. A group in a panel that is a flex box itself takes `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, or what it holds widens the panel.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: One panel. It carries its share of the group, written as its `flex` with `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, so what it holds cannot keep it past its share. Its `overflow` is the design's.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `--panel-size`: The panel's share, in hundredths of the group.
- handle: The bar between two panels: dragged, or moved with the arrows. A design gives it its thickness and `flex-shrink: 0`, so the panels do not squeeze it.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while the bar is dragged.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ScrollArea

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/scroll-area"
```

`<kui-scroll-area>`: `<kui-scroll-area>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `viewport` with its `content`, a `scrollbar` for each way (`kui-orientation="horizontal"` for the one across) with its `thumb`, and a `corner`. A scrollbar is in the page while there is something to scroll its way. The library places the scrollbars and the corner against the root; the page gives a scrollbar its thickness and draws it.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `viewport`
- `content`
- `scrollbar`: `kui-orientation`
- `thumb`: `kui-orientation`
- `corner`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-scroll-area>
  root
    viewport
      content (optional)
      scrollbar (repeated, as above)
    scrollbar (repeated)
      thumb
    corner
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The area. It holds the viewport and the scrollbars, which the library places against it: a design gives a scrollbar its thickness and draws it, and places nothing.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-width`: The width of the corner: the vertical scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-height`: The height of the corner: the horizontal scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
- viewport: The element that scrolls.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
- scrollbar: A scrollbar's track, placed along its edge of the area. In the page while there is something to scroll its way.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while the area is scrolled its way.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-height`: A vertical thumb's height.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-width`: A horizontal thumb's width.
- thumb: The part of a scrollbar that shows where the view is, and can be dragged. As long as its scrollbar's variable says.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.

### Select

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/select"
```

`<kui-select>`: `<kui-select>` around a `kui-part="trigger"` button holding a `value` (it says the chosen item's text, or its `kui-placeholder`; with `multiple`, the chosen items' texts with commas between), and a `portal` with a `positioner` (its `kui-side` and the like, and `kui-align-item-with-trigger`) around the `popup`. The popup holds an `item` for each `kui-value` (`kui-disabled`, `kui-label`), each with an `item-text` and an `item-indicator`; items may be in a `group` with a `group-label`, with `separator`s between, and in a `list` between a `scroll-up-arrow` and a `scroll-down-arrow`. With a name it draws the hidden input a form reads. A `value` part that holds something says what the page wrote there: a `<template kui-each="values">` in it is drawn for each chosen value (`{value}`, `{label}`), in the items' order. `value`, `default-value`, `open`, `default-open`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `multiple`, `values` and `default-values` (with commas between), `name`, `form`; `items` as a property; it tells `value-change`, `values-change` and `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `default-value` (string): The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `open` (boolean): Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: the list still opens to be read, and no item can be chosen. Its value is still submitted with the form.
- `required` (boolean): In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `multiple` (boolean): Several values: an item chosen is added, chosen again taken away, and the list stays open. The values are `values`, not `value`.
- `values` (string): With `multiple`: the chosen values, in the order they were chosen.
- `default-values` (string): With `multiple`: the values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `values`. Read once.
- `name` (string): With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Properties only:

- `items`: The labels of the values, for the trigger to show before the list has ever been opened: a list of values with their labels, or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`). Not needed for the list itself: its items are read from the markup.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `values-change`: `event.detail.values`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `values` as it was.
- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `trigger`
- `value`: `kui-placeholder`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-item-with-trigger`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `list`
- `scroll-up-arrow`
- `scroll-down-arrow`
- `group`: `kui-id`
- `group-label`
- `separator`
- `item`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`, `kui-value`
- `item-text`: `kui-value`
- `item-indicator`: `kui-value`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `values`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-select>
  trigger
    value
      <template kui-each="values"> (optional)
  portal
    positioner
      popup
        scroll-up-arrow
        list (optional)
          group (optional, repeated)
            group-label
            item (repeated)
              item-text
              item-indicator
          separator (repeated)
        scroll-down-arrow
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that shows the value and opens the list.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- value: The chosen value's label, or the placeholder. With several values, their labels with commas between.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
- positioner: Places the list against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- scrollUpArrow: In the page while there is more of the list above: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- scrollDownArrow: In the page while there is more of the list below: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- popup: The list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item, or on each of several.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Separator

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/separator"
```

`<kui-separator>`: `<kui-separator>` around `kui-part="root"`. `orientation`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `orientation` (string): Whether the line lies across (the default) or stands upright: what a screen reader is told.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-separator>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The line.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the line runs.

### Slider

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/slider"
```

`<kui-slider>`: `<kui-slider>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `value` (which says the value as it is written), a `control` with its `track`, `indicator` and a `thumb` for each value, in the values' order (or each with its `kui-index`). A thumb draws the hidden input a form reads. `value` and `default-value` (a range with a comma), `min`, `max`, `step`, `large-step`, `min-steps-between-values`, `thumb-alignment`, `orientation`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `name`, `form`, `locale`; it tells `value-change` and `value-committed`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The value, when the caller holds it: a number, or a list of numbers for a range.
- `default-value` (string): Read once. Default `min`.
- `min` (number): Default 0.
- `max` (number): Default 100.
- `step` (number): Default 1.
- `large-step` (number): What Page Up, Page Down and an arrow with Shift move by. Default 10.
- `min-steps-between-values` (number): How many steps two thumbs of a range stay apart. Default 0.
- `thumb-alignment` (string): Where a thumb is at the ends of its range. `"center"` (the default): its centre on the control's edge, so half of it lies outside. `"edge"`: its edge on the control's edge, so it stays inside. `"edge-client-only"` is the same here: nothing waits for the browser.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the track lies across (the default) or stands upright: the arrows that move a thumb follow.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: no key and no pointer moves a thumb, and its value is still submitted with the form.
- `name` (string): With a name, each thumb's value is submitted with the form around the slider.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `locale` (string): The language a value is written in; the page's by default.

Properties only:

- `format`: How a value is written.
- `getAriaValueText`: What assistive technology reads for a thumb, when the written value is not enough.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.
- `value-committed`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. It reports something that happened: there is nothing to keep.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `value`
- `control`
- `track`
- `indicator`
- `thumb`: `kui-index`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-slider>
  root
    value
    control
      track
        indicator
        thumb (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the slider's parts.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
- control: What a pointer presses and drags on. It holds the track and the thumbs.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
- indicator: The filled part: up to the thumb, or from the first thumb to the last. Its place and length are written on it.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `--start-position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the filled part starts, or with one thumb where it ends.
    - `--relative-size`: With thumbs that stay inside the control and a range: the filled part's length.
- thumb: What is dragged, and what the keyboard moves: a slider to assistive technology. Its place on the track is written on it. It holds a hidden input, which a form reads. A thumb that is given no `index` is the value at its place among the slider's thumbs, in the order they are written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-index`: Which thumb it is, from 0.
    - `--position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the thumb's centre is.

### Switch

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/switch"
```

`<kui-switch>`: `<kui-switch>` around a `kui-part="root"` button with a `thumb` inside. The root draws the hidden native input a form and a label reach. `checked`, `default-checked`, `disabled`, `read-only`, `required`, `name`, `form`, `value`; it tells `checked-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `checked` (boolean): Whether it is checked, when the caller holds it.
- `default-checked` (boolean): Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `read-only` (boolean): Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required` (boolean): Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it unchecked is then invalid.
- `name` (string): With a name, the control is submitted with the form around it when it is checked.
- `form` (string): The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `value` (string): What is submitted. Default `"on"`, as a native checkbox's.
- `kui-id` (string): The id of the switch's hidden native checkbox, not of the switch: a `<label for>` names it. Inside a `Field`, that input takes the field's id instead.

Events:

- `checked-change`: `event.detail.checked`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `checked` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `thumb`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-switch>
  root
    thumb
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The track. It holds a hidden native checkbox, which a form and a label reach.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
- thumb: The knob that moves along the track.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.

### Tabs

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/tabs"
```

`<kui-tabs>`: `<kui-tabs>` around `kui-part="root"`, a `list` with a `tab` for each `value` and an `indicator`, and a `panel` for each `value`, in the page while its tab is the active one. `value`, `default-value`, `orientation`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The active tab's value; `null` is "none".
- `default-value` (string): Read once. Without one, the first tab that can be chosen is, once the page is there.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the tabs are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `list`
- `indicator`
- `tab`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-value`
- `panel`: `kui-value`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-tabs>
  root
    list
      tab (repeated)
      indicator
    panel (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the tabs and their panels.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- list: The row of tabs. The arrows move between them.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- tab: A button that shows its panel.
    - `data-active`: Present on the tab whose panel is shown.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
- indicator: A mark for the active tab: it carries that tab's position and size.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
    - `--active-tab-left`: The active tab's distance from the list's left edge.
    - `--active-tab-right`: The active tab's distance from the list's right edge.
    - `--active-tab-top`: The active tab's distance from the list's top edge.
    - `--active-tab-bottom`: The active tab's distance from the list's bottom edge.
    - `--active-tab-width`: The active tab's width.
    - `--active-tab-height`: The active tab's height.
- panel: A tab's content. In the page while its tab is active, and through its exit.
    - `data-hidden`: Present while its tab is not the active one.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Toast

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/toast"
```

`<kui-toast>`: `<kui-toast>` around a `kui-part="viewport"`, which holds a `<template kui-each="toasts">` with a `toast` for each message (`{id}`, `{type}`), its `content` with a `title` and a `description`, and a `close` and an `action` button. A `title`, a `description` and an `action` written empty say what the toast was added with, and are in the page only for a toast that has one; one written with something in it (`{title}`) is always there. `label`, `hotkey`, `swipe-direction`; `duration` and `limit` for the toaster it makes, or `toaster` as a property for one of the page's own. A title, a description and an action's label are strings.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `label` (string)
- `hotkey` (string)
- `swipe-direction` (string)
- `duration` (number)
- `limit` (number)

Properties only:

- `toaster`

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `viewport`
- `toast`
- `content`
- `title`
- `description`
- `close`
- `action`

Lists (`<template kui-each="…">`): `toasts`.

Anatomy:

```
<kui-toast>
  viewport
    <template kui-each="toasts">
      toast (repeated)
        content (optional)
          title
          description
        close
        action
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- viewport: Where the toasts are drawn: a region that is always in the page.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
    - `--toast-frontmost-height`: The height of the newest toast.
- root: One toast.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
    - `data-limited`: Present on a toast behind as many as are shown at once.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the toast is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-direction="left | right | up | down"`: The way the toast was dragged out, once it has been.
    - `--toast-index`: Its place in the stack: 0 for the newest.
    - `--toast-height`: Its height.
    - `--toast-offset-y`: The height of the toasts in front of it.
    - `--toast-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--toast-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
- content: What holds a toast's contents, when the design sizes the toast itself.
    - `data-behind`: Present on a toast that is behind the newest.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.

### Toggle

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/toggle"
```

`<kui-toggle>`: `<kui-toggle>` around a `kui-part="root"` button. Inside a `<kui-toggle-group>` it is one of the group's, by its `value`; inside a `<kui-toolbar>`, one of its items. `pressed`, `default-pressed`, `disabled`, `value`; it tells `pressed-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `pressed` (boolean): Whether it is pressed, when the caller holds it.
- `default-pressed` (boolean): Read once.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: a press does nothing.
- `value` (string): In a toggle group: what the group's value holds while this one is pressed.

Events:

- `pressed-change`: `event.detail.pressed`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `pressed` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-toggle>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The button. It stays pressed until it is pressed again.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while it is pressed.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ToggleGroup

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/toggle-group"
```

`<kui-toggle-group>`: `<kui-toggle-group>` around `kui-part="root"` and its `<kui-toggle>`s, each with a `value`. `value` and `default-value` (the pressed ones, with commas between), `multiple`, `disabled`, `orientation`, `loop`; it tells `value-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `value` (string): The values of the pressed toggles: none, one, or with `multiple` several.
- `default-value` (string): The values pressed at the start, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `multiple` (boolean): Whether more than one can be pressed at a time.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables every toggle of the group.
- `orientation` (string): Whether the toggles are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `loop` (boolean): Whether the arrows go round from the last toggle to the first. Default: they do.

Events:

- `value-change`: `event.detail.value`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `value` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-toggle-group>
  root
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group. A toggle inside it with a `value` is one of its toggles.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether its toggles are in a row or a column.
    - `data-multiple`: Present when several can be pressed at a time.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Toolbar

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/toolbar"
```

`<kui-toolbar>`: `<kui-toolbar>` around `kui-part="root"` and its items: a `button`, a `link`, an `input`, a `group`, a `separator` (`kui-disabled` on one that is off), and `<kui-toggle>`s and `<kui-toggle-group>`s, which are the toolbar's items too. One stop for Tab; the arrows move between them. `orientation`, `loop`, `disabled`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `orientation` (string): Whether the controls are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `loop` (boolean): Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disables every control of the toolbar.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `root`
- `button`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`
- `input`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`
- `group`: `kui-disabled`, `kui-label`
- `link`
- `separator`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-toolbar>
  root
    group (optional, repeated)
      button (repeated)
      link (repeated)
      input (repeated)
    separator (repeated)
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The toolbar. It is one stop for Tab.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- button: A button of the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- link: A link of the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: A text input of the toolbar. The arrows are its own until the caret is at an end.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- group: Items that belong together.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- separator: A line between items, across the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.

### Tooltip

```
import "@kirana-ui/web/tooltip"
```

`<kui-tooltip>`: `<kui-tooltip>` around a `kui-part="trigger"` and a `portal` with a `positioner` (its `kui-side` and the like) around the `popup`, which may hold an `arrow`. `open`, `default-open`, `delay`, `close-delay`, `disabled`; it tells `open-change`.

Attributes of the element (each also a property, in camel case):

- `open` (boolean): Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `default-open` (boolean): Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `delay` (number): How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds.
- `close-delay` (number): How long after the pointer leaves the popup closes, in milliseconds.
- `disabled` (boolean): Disabled: the pointer and focus do not open it.

Events:

- `open-change`: `event.detail.open`, with `event.detail.details`. `preventDefault()` keeps `open` as it was.

Parts (`kui-part`), each with the `kui-` attributes its element is read for:

- `trigger`: `kui-close-delay`, `kui-delay`
- `positioner`: `kui-align`, `kui-align-offset`, `kui-anchor`, `kui-arrow-padding`, `kui-collision-boundary`, `kui-collision-padding`, `kui-position-method`, `kui-side`, `kui-side-offset`, `kui-sticky`
- `popup`
- `arrow`

Anatomy:

```
<kui-tooltip>
  trigger
  portal
    positioner
      popup
        arrow
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The element the tooltip describes.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the tooltip is open.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The tooltip itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="delay | focus | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed without its usual wait, for a design that skips the motion then.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.
